newsitem.title: USA: Interface says to reduce expenses.
newsitem.headline: Interface says to reduce expenses.

text.p: Interface Systems Inc's president and chief executive officer said Monday he plans to align expenses with revenues the company can realistically expect.
"We are determined to act throughout the company with greater speed as a prerequisite to success in today's software markets," President and CEO Robert Nero said in a statement.

Nero did not describe any specific actions. His statement came after the firm reported a fiscal first quarter loss of $725,053, or $0.16 a share, versus a profit of $200,024 or $0.05 in the year-ago period.
"Expense levels in our core product business are still too high in the U.S. and in the UK considering the lack of revenue growth," Nero said.

Revenues rose in the UK distribution business and were up slightly in the Oasis business, but fell in other core product areas from year-ago levels. Total fiscal first quarter revenues were $19.6 million, up from $18.7 million last year.
Interface sells document management, presentation and connectivity products for computer systems.
